title: Therapies that drive the whole clonal population to extinction

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a way to design cancer treatment that eliminates the entire malignant population, including cells that are initially sensitive, resistant lineages already present before treatment, and surviving cells capable of developing resistance later. It could take the form of a drug combination, a treatment sequence, or a rule for choosing and timing therapies. Its defining outcome would be elimination of every lineage capable of restarting the cancer.

This requires treating a tumor as an evolving population. Treatment can remove most cells while leaving rare resistant cells or drug-tolerant persisters that subsequently regenerate the disease. Persisters need not carry a detectable resistance mutation: reversible changes in cell state can permit survival and provide a route toward more durable resistance. Consequently, eliminating known resistant genotypes alone would not establish that the whole population had been extinguished.

significance.text: In many treated advanced or metastatic tumors, an initial response leaves residual populations capable of regrowth. The May 2025 review by Liu and colleagues describes this persister problem and emphasizes that most patients in the advanced or metastatic setting remain incurable. A treatment principle that reliably removes both the initial population and its routes of escape could turn some temporary responses into durable eradication.

Conditional synthesis: if such a principle worked across multiple cancers, its importance would extend beyond any single drug. It could guide combinations and sequences that make successive survival routes lethal or unavailable. Continued regression after the initially sensitive population has been depleted would be an important intermediate consequence; durable elimination of all surviving lineages would remain the decisive outcome. Wider applicability would have to be demonstrated across defined tumor types and resistance mechanisms.

The evolutionary-control analogy has practical limits. A model or scheduling rule cannot itself kill cells: the regimen still needs active treatments, tolerable exposure, and access to every relevant disease site. Genetic evolution, epigenetic adaptation, and changes in cell identity create different survival routes, and one surviving lineage capable of regrowth could defeat eradication. Plastic or stem-like states are possible escape mechanisms within this problem, rather than evidence for a universal cancer stem-cell marker.

Conditional synthesis: sustained containment could still provide substantial clinical benefit. Maintaining stable disease through dose modulation or managing competition between populations would, however, answer a different question from whether the cancer population had become extinct. Likewise, a response or survival improvement would establish benefit without, by itself, resolving whether any surviving malignant lineage remained.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target capability is a regimen that eliminates pre-existing resistant lineages and persisters capable of generating resistance, while also eliminating the initially sensitive population. The supplied evidence establishes this as a scientific and therapeutic challenge. It does not establish a comprehensive field-wide absence of such demonstrations as of November 1, 2026.

A central biological barrier is that surviving populations can resist several modes of attack at once. In the laboratory models reported by Davern and colleagues, immunotherapy persisters showed reduced sensitivity to multiple drug classes and radiotherapy. Drug-tolerant persisters showed reduced sensitivity to drugs and radiotherapy and additionally to T-cell killing. Both populations showed reduced sensitivity to mitochondrial apoptosis, a major pathway through which cells execute programmed death. These findings suggest that switching treatment modality may leave shared survival mechanisms intact.

Another barrier is the relationship between reversible tolerance and lasting resistance. Residual cells can survive through non-genetic adaptation, proliferate without detectable genomic mutations, and later acquire more stable resistance. A successful regimen would therefore need to address changing phenotypes as well as identifiable resistant clones. The review links epigenetic plasticity with genetic evolution and discusses dedifferentiation and stem-like states as contributors to recurrence.

Engineering synthesis: the treatment problem also includes choosing combinations and timing that close escape routes without intolerable injury to normal tissues, maintaining effective exposure across disease sites, and measuring residual populations well enough to guide decisions. The measurement problem is especially demanding: disappearance from scans or sampled tissue can coexist with rare, unsampled survivors. Treatment design and evidence of extinction must therefore address spatial coverage, detection limits, and changing cell states together.

current_state.text: Liu and colleagues’ review, published May 24, 2025 in Molecular Cancer, describes drug-tolerant persisters, their relationship to recurrence and resistance, and therapeutic approaches intended to kill them, promote immune-mediated elimination, or prevent resistant clones from arising. It explicitly cautions that much of the underlying evidence comes from preclinical models with limited clinical validation in human cohorts. The supplied review assessment used a PDF extraction truncated on page 30 of 32; the relevant mechanistic discussion, limitations, and cited therapeutic goals were intact.

Davern and colleagues’ study, reported as published online December 26, 2025 in Cell Death & Differentiation, provides laboratory evidence of the cross-resistance and reduced apoptotic sensitivity described above. Its abstract also reports that targeting anti-apoptotic dependencies increased persister sensitivity to chemotherapy or CAR T therapy. This supports apoptosis sensitization as a candidate countermeasure, but increased sensitivity is not a demonstration of complete elimination in patients. The supplied evidence covers the PubMed abstract; full experimental methods and figures were not available for assessment.

The research notes attribute the following results to a 2026 phase 1–2 report of the multi-selective RAS(ON) inhibitor daraxonrasib: among 26 previously treated people with RAS G12-mutant pancreatic cancer receiving 300 mg, an objective response rate of 35%, median duration of response of 8.2 months, and median progression-free survival of 8.5 months. These figures remain unverified within the supplied evidence. Although the notes describe abstract-level access, no source text was retained for the supplied review to check the cohort, dose, outcomes, or publication details. They should therefore be read as attributed numerical claims rather than confirmed trial findings in this record.

The notes also attribute a seven-month improvement in median overall survival versus chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer to the later RASolute 302 trial, as described in a November 2026 Lancet Oncology comment. Neither the comment text nor the underlying trial report was retained for assessment. The November issue designation alone does not establish availability by November 1, 2026. The magnitude, population, and timing of this reported benefit consequently remain unresolved here.

The supplied review and persister abstract establish mechanisms and candidate countermeasures; neither demonstrates clinical extinction of the whole resistant clonal population in common metastatic carcinomas. The supplied search record contains no results from which to establish the field’s complete status through November 1, 2026. Missing clinical source material is an evidence limitation, not evidence that the attributed results are false. Even if the reported response and survival benefits are confirmed, separate residual-disease and lineage evidence would be needed to assess extinction; aggregate survival gains alone would neither prove nor disprove eradication in particular patients.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: prospectively test a specified regimen in metastatic cancers where the starting targeted therapy is known to select resistance. Show continued regression after the initially sensitive population has been depleted, followed by sustained disappearance of detectable disease. Specify how depletion and disappearance will be measured. These would be proposed evidentiary criteria for this innovation, not established clinical standards, and continued regression alone would be insufficient.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained disease disappearance following regression beyond sensitive population depletion

completion_criteria.text: Proposed lineage and cell-state assessment: track resistant genotypes present before treatment and newly emerging genotypes through serial sampling, complemented by assays for non-genetic persister states. Prespecify spatial sampling coverage, assay detection limits, and the handling of inaccessible lesions or inconclusive samples. Genotype tracking is necessary for some escape routes but cannot by itself exclude rare unsampled lineages or phenotypic survival without detectable genomic change.
completion_criteria.label: Resistant lineages and persister states tracked within prespecified sampling limits

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and reproducibility requirements: use a justified follow-up period, report recurrence and residual-disease findings, and reproduce the result in independent cohorts. Where treatment withdrawal is clinically appropriate, sustained absence of detectable disease after therapy ends would strengthen the case for eradication. Continued treatment could otherwise be suppressing survivors. No finite follow-up or sampling scheme can directly prove that every malignant cell is absent.
completion_criteria.label: Durable disease disappearance reproduced in independent cohorts with justified follow-up

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: establish tolerability, effective delivery across relevant disease sites, and reproducibility across clearly described tumor types and resistance mechanisms. A successful finite test would establish the demonstrated breadth of the approach, not literal universality. Prolonged stable disease through dose modulation would demonstrate valuable containment, while remaining short of the extinction goal.
completion_criteria.label: Tolerable, effective delivery reproduced across defined tumors and resistance mechanisms

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: ONC-02, “Sterilizing immune clearance of established metastatic carcinomas,” overlaps directly in its desired eradication outcome but specifies immune clearance as the route. ONC-05 concerns treatment design across possible modalities. ONC-12, “Off-the-shelf cell therapy that matches autologous cures and can be given at ordinary scale,” concerns the efficacy and scalability of a particular therapeutic platform. Such cells might contribute to an extinction regimen, but scalable manufacture and complete elimination of escape-capable populations are distinct achievements.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-03, “Eradication of dormant disseminated tumor cells that cause late relapse,” focuses on a particular residual population and its delayed consequences. Dormant cells could fall within ONC-05 whenever they can restart the cancer, but ONC-05 also encompasses actively growing resistant clones and treatment-induced persister states. Dormancy, drug tolerance, and genetic resistance should not be treated as interchangeable.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-04, “A shared malignant dependency that renewing normal tissues can spare,” could supply a broadly useful target for an extinction regimen. A shared dependency would still need to remain vulnerable in surviving populations under treatment. ONC-07, “Body-wide delivery that alters essentially every malignant cell,” addresses access and coverage, which could be necessary for eradication but would not establish that the delivered intervention kills every escape-capable lineage.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-06, “Stable reversion of carcinoma cells to non-malignant tissue identity,” seeks lasting removal of malignant behavior through a change of identity. It could share an ultimate goal of preventing malignant regrowth, but it does not necessarily eliminate the treated cellular lineages. ONC-05 instead centers on extinction of the malignant population. Plastic and stem-like states connect these questions biologically without making the two innovations equivalent.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-01, “Mortality-reducing detection of lethal cancers while they are still localized,” and ONC-10, “A reliable distinction between early neoplasms that will kill and those that will not,” concern earlier identification and selection of disease requiring intervention. ONC-11, “Real-time, cell-resolution guidance that makes incomplete cancer surgery uncommon,” concerns completeness of local removal. These advances could reduce the burden requiring systemic treatment, while ONC-05 addresses surviving and evolving malignant populations, particularly in established metastatic disease.

Roster-based synthesis: ONC-08, “Interception of non-viral precancers before they invade,” and ONC-09, “Prophylactic immunity that prevents the common non-viral cancers,” act before invasive cancer or its establishment. They could reduce how often an extinction therapy is needed. Their preventive endpoints remain distinct from eliminating an existing heterogeneous malignant population.

change_log.change: Preserved ONC-05 and its title while defining the innovation around elimination of all regrowth-capable malignant populations.
change_log.reason: The central concept remains useful even though the supplied material does not demonstrate its achievement or establish a complete field-wide status.

change_log.change: Narrowed the recurrence claim to many treated advanced or metastatic tumors and made the revolutionary impact explicitly conditional.
change_log.reason: The review supports persister-mediated recurrence and major unmet need, without establishing a universal recurrence pattern or inevitable success.

change_log.change: Corrected the persister study attribution to Davern and colleagues and separated the findings for immunotherapy persisters and drug-tolerant persisters.
change_log.reason: The supplied abstract identifies Davern-led authorship and reports asymmetric cross-resistance findings, with reduced mitochondrial apoptotic sensitivity in both populations.

change_log.change: Integrated reversible tolerance, genetic evolution, cell-identity plasticity, and shared apoptotic resistance into the scientific barriers.
change_log.reason: These distinctions explain why eliminating known resistant genotypes or switching treatment modalities may leave routes to regrowth.

change_log.change: Separated continued regression, clinical benefit, containment, and extinction.
change_log.reason: Each is a different outcome; regression or a median survival improvement cannot alone establish elimination of all surviving lineages.

change_log.change: Retained the daraxonrasib and RASolute 302 numerical claims only as explicitly unverified attributions, including their cohort, dose, outcome measures, and access limitations.
change_log.reason: The request requires preserving quantitative detail when unresolved. No retained clinical source text supports treating these figures as confirmed, but its absence does not show they are false.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed demonstration to include emergent genotypes, non-genetic persisters, spatial coverage, detection limits, durability, independent reproduction, and practical tolerability.
change_log.reason: Baseline sequencing and continued regression alone cannot distinguish undetected survivors from eradication. These additions are proposals rather than published consensus thresholds.

change_log.change: Added explicit distinctions with all other supplied roster entries and preserved the review’s access and extraction limitations.
change_log.reason: Related mechanisms and enabling technologies should remain separate concepts, and evidence scope must remain visible where it limits interpretation.

unresolved_issues: The daraxonrasib phase 1–2 source has no retained text. The identity, cohort of 26, 300 mg dose, 35% response rate, 8.2-month median response duration, and 8.5-month median progression-free survival remain unverified in this record.

The reported seven-month RASolute 302 median overall-survival advantage lacks retained comment or trial text. Its exact population, comparison, magnitude, and availability by November 1, 2026 remain unresolved.

The review’s recommendation to remove the uninspectable clinical numbers was not adopted literally because the requested final record calls for preserving unresolved quantitative detail with explicit qualification. The figures are retained as attributed claims, not established findings.
An empty supplied search record cannot establish whether any relevant extinction demonstration existed elsewhere by November 1, 2026.
The Davern evidence is limited to an abstract, so experimental methods, model-specific boundaries, and full results cannot be independently assessed from the supplied material.
The appropriate sampling coverage, detection limits, follow-up duration, and evidence needed to distinguish durable suppression from eradication remain to be specified for any actual trial.
The breadth, tolerability, and feasibility of a regimen that closes genetic and non-genetic escape routes across all relevant disease sites remain open scientific and engineering questions.

brief.title: Treatment that kills every cancer cell able to regrow
possible: People with cancer could receive treatment designed to eliminate every cancer cell capable of restarting the disease. It would kill cells that respond at first, cells already resistant to treatment, and survivors that could develop resistance later.
Doctors could use a combination of treatments, a sequence, or a rule for timing them to close the cancer’s escape routes. The goal would be lasting elimination of the disease.
why: For people with advanced cancer, an initial response can leave surviving cells that rebuild the disease. Eliminating those survivors could turn some temporary responses into lasting eradication.

A treatment principle that worked across several cancers could guide choices beyond any single drug. It could help doctors choose combinations and sequences that make successive routes of survival unavailable.

sources.showed: Their review describes persisters: cancer cells that survive treatment through changes that can be reversible. It brings together research on how these cells survive, restart tumors and become vulnerable to treatment.
sources.quote: Initial therapies eliminate the bulk of tumor cells, yet residual populations termed drug-tolerant persister cells (DTPs) survive, regenerate tumor and even drive distant metastases.
sources.cited_for: Survivors can restart cancer without initially carrying a lasting genetic change that causes resistance.
sources.not_established: Much of the research comes from laboratory models, with limited testing in patients.

sources.showed: In laboratory models, cells surviving drugs or immune treatments resisted several other treatments and became less sensitive to programmed cell death. Targeting their defenses against cell death increased treatment sensitivity.
sources.quote: Targeting anti-apoptotic dependencies in persisters increased sensitivity to chemotherapy or CAR T therapy.
sources.cited_for: Different treatments can leave survivors with shared defenses, offering a possible target for further treatment.
sources.not_established: Greater treatment sensitivity in laboratory models does not establish complete elimination in patients.

sources.who: Authors of the daraxonrasib trial report
sources.showed: This is an early clinical trial report on daraxonrasib in previously treated pancreatic cancer.
sources.cited_for: The report concerns a candidate treatment for previously treated pancreatic cancer.
sources.not_established: Tumor responses alone would not establish that every cancer cell capable of regrowth had been eliminated.

sources.showed: This is a commentary on a trial comparing treatment with chemotherapy in previously treated pancreatic cancer that had spread.
sources.cited_for: The commentary concerns a reported survival benefit in advanced pancreatic cancer.
sources.not_established: Longer survival alone would not establish that no surviving cancer cells could restart the disease.

shown: Davern and colleagues found a shared weakness in laboratory models: targeting survivors’ defenses against programmed cell death made them more sensitive to treatment. They also found that survivors of one treatment could resist other kinds of attack.

Liu and colleagues describe several approaches to killing persisters or preventing lasting resistance. Much of this work remains in laboratory models. These findings support possible treatment strategies, but do not demonstrate elimination of every surviving cancer cell in patients.
missing: A regimen still needs to demonstrate elimination of initially sensitive cells, existing resistant cells and persisters able to develop resistance.
Treatment must reach all relevant disease sites at effective levels without intolerable harm to healthy tissue.
Measurements must address rare survivors, inaccessible disease sites and cells that survive without detectable genetic changes.
Independent patient groups must show lasting disease disappearance with follow-up that can distinguish elimination from continued suppression.

milestones.label: Disease stays absent after regression continues beyond sensitive cell loss
milestones.explanation: A trial would have to show continued shrinkage after initially sensitive cells are depleted, followed by sustained disappearance of detectable disease. This would test whether treatment reaches beyond the first responding cells.

milestones.label: Resistant cell families and persister states are tracked
milestones.explanation: Repeated sampling would have to track resistant cancer cell families and persister states, with sampling coverage and detection limits set beforehand. This would test whether different routes of survival remain.

milestones.label: Independent patient groups show lasting disease disappearance
milestones.explanation: Independent patient groups would have to show lasting disappearance with justified follow-up and tests for remaining disease. Absence after treatment ends, where appropriate, would strengthen the case that survivors were eliminated.

milestones.label: Safe, effective delivery works across defined cancers
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to reproduce tolerable treatment and effective delivery across disease sites, defined cancers and resistance mechanisms. This would establish how broadly the approach works.

uncertain: How much sampling and follow-up would distinguish eradication from suppression, given that neither can prove every cancer cell is gone?
Can treatment close both genetic and reversible survival routes without intolerable harm?
How broadly could a successful regimen work across cancers and resistance mechanisms?

page.title: Cancer extinction therapy
page.definition: A treatment eliminates every malignant lineage capable of regenerating a particular advanced solid cancer at any site. In a first-strike, second-strike regimen, the first treatment reduces the size and diversity of the cancer population. A different treatment targets the survivors while their numbers are low, before regrowth. Survivors can include cells already resistant to the first drug and drug-tolerant persisters, which survive in a reversible state.

goal.need: In Norway in 2015, metastases were recorded as a contributing cause in 6,483 deaths from solid tumours, 66.7% of the total. In previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, median time to progression or death was 7.2 months with daraxonrasib and 3.6 months with chemotherapy. Even when tumours shrink, surviving cells can regrow. Eliminating those cells at every site, at doses patients can tolerate, would spare patients a recurrence of that cancer and further treatment for it.

statements.quote: Blocking or exploiting such switching processes could inhibit the recurrence of cancer and eliminate resistant cells after successful primary treatment.
statements.context: The cancer-cell-plasticity challenge concerns changes of cellular identity that contribute to treatment resistance.

statements.quote: By understanding the mechanisms regulating tumour dormancy, can we develop approaches to eradicate dormant cells, or prevent their re-emergence?
statements.context: The dormancy challenge concerns residual cancer cells after apparently successful treatment.

statements.body: Moffitt Cancer Center extinction-therapy developers, Gatenby and colleagues
statements.quote: We propose integrating the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of extinction into treatment protocols with curative intent.
statements.context: Published online on 26 November 2019; the paper presents a treatment hypothesis supported by mathematical models and simulations.

statements.body: H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center and Research Institute, METTSEO protocol
statements.quote: attempting to make extinct, resulting in a cure for the patient
statements.context: The protocol applies successive treatments to residual cancer cells in widely metastatic Ewing sarcoma. Its primary objective is to determine whether patients can complete the planned treatment schedule.

completion.title: Treatment eliminates every malignant lineage capable of regenerating a defined advanced solid cancer.
completion.criterion: After treatment, no initially sensitive, pre-existing resistant or persister-derived malignant lineage remains capable of regenerating the cancer. This is a biological endpoint without an established finite clinical verification test. Imaging disappearance, undetectable sampled tumour DNA, prolonged remission and survival improvement do not individually establish it. None of the cited persister-directed clinical results demonstrates whole-population extinction.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no externally validated clinical test of whole-population malignant-lineage extinction was located.
completion.basis: Searches covered FDA oncology endpoint guidance, RECIST, NCI cure definitions, Cancer Grand Challenges, extinction-therapy papers and the registered first-strike/second-strike prostate-cancer protocol. They yielded response, survival and remission endpoints, but no validated sampling depth, follow-up duration or assay establishing extinction of every malignant lineage. The criterion therefore retains the narrow biological meaning of extinction.

milestones.title: Trichostatin A selectively kills PC9 lung-cancer persisters in a 20-hour assay.
milestones.criterion: Plate parental PC9 cells and PC9-derived drug-tolerant persisters at equal density. Compare untreated cultures with cultures exposed to trichostatin A for 20 hours. Use flow cytometry to measure the fraction of cells with sub-G1 DNA content, a marker of cell death. The increase over the untreated control must be greater in persisters than in parental cells.
milestones.set_by: Sharma and colleagues, Massachusetts General Hospital Cancer Center; Figure 4B experimental protocol, written for PC9 lung-cancer cells.
milestones.threshold_quote: treated with the indicated TSA concentrations for 20 hours

milestones.title: TROP2 CAR T cells delay regrowth beyond 400 mm³ in an EGFR-mutant lung-cancer xenograft.
milestones.criterion: In mice bearing DFCI-243 patient-derived tumours, give osimertinib through day 42 and introduce TROP2-directed CAR T cells or sacituzumab govitecan on day 22. Compare relapse-free survival between groups. Relapse is regrowth beyond 400 mm³ after the tumour has reached minimal residual disease. The CAR T-cell group must have longer relapse-free survival than the sacituzumab govitecan group.
milestones.set_by: Baldacci and colleagues, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; xenograft relapse endpoint and treatment comparison, written for EGFR-mutant lung cancer.
milestones.threshold_quote: prevent disease relapse, defined as when tumors reach >400 mm^{3} after achieving MRD.

milestones.title: At least half the patients complete three cycles with more than 75% of each drug’s planned dose.
milestones.criterion: In the ETCTN 9903 dose-expansion cohort with EGFR T790M-positive lung cancer, at least 50% of patients must complete three 28-day cycles while receiving more than 75% of the planned total dose of each drug, osimertinib and navitoclax.
milestones.set_by: National Cancer Institute, ETCTN 9903, NCT02520778, registered dose-expansion feasibility endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: The proportion of patients completing 3 courses of therapy with > 75% of total dose of each drug will be quantified.

milestones.title: The assayed EGFR mutations become undetectable in plasma after two treatment cycles.
milestones.criterion: Evaluate patients with a detectable EGFR mutation in pretreatment plasma. Test plasma by droplet digital PCR for the known sensitizing mutation, either L858R or an exon 19 deletion, and for T790M. A complete circulating tumour DNA response requires that none of the assayed EGFR mutations be detectable after two cycles.
milestones.set_by: ETCTN 9903 investigators; published EGFR-mutant lung-cancer biomarker endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: no detectable EGFR mutation after 2 cycles

milestones.title: Non-nodal lesions disappear and all pathological nodes measure under 10 mm in short axis.
milestones.criterion: For an overall complete response under RECIST 1.1, all non-nodal target and non-target lesions must disappear, all pathological nodes must measure less than 10 mm in short axis, initially elevated tumour markers must normalize, and no new lesion may appear. In a nonrandomized trial with response as its primary endpoint, confirm the response on repeat assessment.
milestones.set_by: RECIST Working Group, revised RECIST guideline version 1.1, sections 4.3.1–4.3.4 and Table 1.
milestones.threshold_quote: Any pathological lymph nodes (whether target or non-target) must have reduction in short axis to <10 mm.

milestones.title: A complete remission persists for at least five years.
milestones.criterion: All signs and symptoms of cancer remain absent for at least five years. NCI describes this as a convention under which some doctors may use the word cured, while explicitly warning that surviving cells can cause later recurrence. The convention does not require treatment withdrawal and cannot distinguish eradication from continued suppression. It is the nearest finite clinical convention located, rather than a verified final step to whole-lineage extinction.
milestones.set_by: Clinical convention described by the National Cancer Institute in Cancer Prognosis; not an NCI certification of eradication.
milestones.threshold_quote: If you remain in complete remission for 5 years or more, some doctors may say that you are cured.

milestones.title: Three-year event-free survival reaches 35% in metastatic fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
milestones.criterion: In the second-strike arm of NCT04388839, estimate event-free survival three years from treatment initiation in newly diagnosed metastatic PAX/FOXO1 fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma. An event is local, regional or distant recurrence, or death from any cause. Compare the estimate with the protocol’s 35% target.
milestones.set_by: Moffitt Cancer Center, NCT04388839, three-year event-free survival objective and second-strike arm endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: 3-year event-free survival (EFS) from its current 6% to 35% in metastatic, fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma patients.

not_found: No validated finite clinical test of extinction of every malignant lineage was found in the searched regulatory, committee or protocol sources.
No common preclinical eradication cutoff or lineage-wide residual-disease assay standard for advanced solid cancers was found.
No externally defined final intermediate result was found that bridges prolonged clinical remission to verified whole-population extinction.
Davern and colleagues’ full experimental methods and sample sizes were inaccessible; the abstract and figure descriptions were available.
The supplied Lancet Oncology commentary could not be opened.
No oncology society or cancer programme statement rejecting malignant-lineage extinction as a therapeutic goal was found.

results.finding: PC9-derived persisters showed a greater 20-hour trichostatin A-induced increase in sub-G1 cells than parental PC9 cells in 2 independent experiments.
results.detail: Figure 4B upper panel. The supplied text gives the direction of the effect and the experiment count. The measured percentages are plotted in the figure.
results.quote: caused the rapid death of DTPs and DTEPs, but did not detectably affect parental PC9 cells or TKI re-sensitized DTEPs

results.finding: M14 melanoma persisters showed a greater sub-G1 response than parental M14 cells after 36 hours of trichostatin A in 2 experiments.
results.detail: Figure 4C upper panel. The measured sub-G1 percentages are plotted in the figure.
results.quote: Similarly, drug-tolerant populations of M14, Colo205, HCC827, and HT-29 cancer cell lines also demonstrated TSA hypersensitivity

results.finding: Cisplatin-tolerant COLO 205 cells showed a greater sub-G1 response to trichostatin A than parental cells at the 36-hour readout in 2 experiments.
results.detail: Figure 4D gives the readout time relative to plating. The measured sub-G1 percentages are plotted in the figure.
results.quote: Similarly, drug-tolerant populations of M14, Colo205, HCC827, and HT-29 cancer cell lines also demonstrated TSA hypersensitivity

results.finding: DFCI-243 xenografts (10 mice per group) had median relapse-free survival >200 days with TROP2 CAR T cells.
results.detail: The CAR T-cell group received a single infusion, and the sacituzumab govitecan group received repeated doses.
results.quote: the TROP2 CAR-T group exhibited a median RFS of >200 days (p=0.0014 compared to sacituzumab govitecan)

results.finding: Seven of nine patients in the T790M-positive expansion cohort received >95% of planned combination doses through three cycles.
results.detail: The planned daily doses were 80 mg osimertinib and 150 mg navitoclax, both starting on cycle 1 day 1.
results.quote: Seven of nine patients (78%) received >95% of planned doses through 3 cycles

results.finding: All seven evaluable expansion patients cleared detectable plasma EGFR mutations after two cycles.
results.quote:
All 7 evaluable patients in the dose expansion cohort demonstrated a complete ctDNA response with no detectable
EGFR
mutation after 2 cycles

results.finding: One of nine T790M-positive expansion patients achieved a RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.detail: The paper reports the overall response classification. Individual lesion measurements and tumour-marker values for the responder are absent from the supplied text.
results.quote: In the dose expansion phase (n=9), the objective response rate (ORR) was 100%, including one complete response (11%) and eight partial responses (89%)

results.finding: Among 226 patients with metastatic melanoma enrolled in ACT-TIL trials, 49 achieved a complete response.
results.quote: The overall response rate was 51% (116/226) with a complete response rate of 22% (49/226).

results.finding: In the 34-patient PD-1-refractory melanoma cohort, one patient had an ongoing complete remission at 84 months.
results.quote: One patient whose tumors progressed after eight months of dual checkpoint blockade prior to ACT-TIL achieved the only durable complete response (84 months, ongoing) in this population (

results.finding: In a review of 432 patients with stage IV cutaneous melanoma, 59 had complete remission lasting more than five years after starting immunotherapy.
results.detail: Some patients also received surgery or radiation for metastatic disease. For progression-free survival, follow-up was timed from immunotherapy initiation or the last such local treatment, whichever came later.
results.quote: Thus, the focus of our study is limited to the 59 patients who survived in complete remission for more than 5 years after starting immunotherapy.

results.finding: In CheckMate 8HW, 30% of 296 patients with metastatic colorectal cancer had a complete response to nivolumab plus ipilimumab.
results.detail: The paper reports complete responses by RECIST 1.1 category and provides aggregate counts.
results.quote:
Complete responses were 
reported in 90 (30%) of 296 patients in the nivolumab plus 
ipilimumab group and 80 (28%) of 286 patients in the 
nivolumab group

results.finding: After GD2 CAR T-cell therapy, 3 of 11 children with active neuroblastoma achieved a complete response.
results.quote: Of 11 patients with active disease at infusion, three achieved a complete response that was sustained in two patients, one for 8 years until lost to follow-up and one for more than 18 years.

results.finding: Among 11 children with active neuroblastoma at infusion, 2 remained in complete remission for at least five years after GD2 CAR T-cell therapy.
results.quote: Of 11 patients with active disease at infusion, three achieved a complete response that was sustained in two patients, one for 8 years until lost to follow-up and one for more than 18 years.

results.finding: One patient with relapsed PAX3–FOXO1 fusion-positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma had a reported complete response at day 78.
results.detail: The reported complete response and target-node resolution bear on the milestone. The article does not identify RECIST 1.1 as the assessment standard or document every component of the criterion.

results.finding: Metastatic CIC-rearranged sarcoma (n=10 treated): 1 RECIST 1.1 complete response to first-line chemotherapy.
results.detail: The responder had lung-only metastases and received adjuvant VDC/IE after an R1 resection.
results.quote: Among metastatic patients, 10 (83%) received chemotherapy (1 CR, 5 PR, 2 MR, 1 PD); 9 died (one without chemotherapy).

results.finding: Among 1,115 patients with measurable metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, 10 had a reported RECIST 1.1 complete response.
results.detail: Table 2 reports best response by arm. Patient-level tumour-marker results at complete response are unavailable in the supplied text.

results.finding: Recurrent EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (n=1) remained in complete remission for 10 years after gefitinib withdrawal.
results.detail: CT showed disappearance of the recurrent supraclavicular nodes after 3 months. Gefitinib was stopped after 18 months because of a grade 3 rash.
results.quote: Complete response has continued throughout, during and even after termination of gefitinib treatment. The patient has received no additional anti-tumor treatment and is still alive without tumor 10 years after the termination of gefitinib treatment.

results.finding: One patient with hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer had 10 years without observed progression on letrozole.
results.detail: After vinorelbine, the palpable breast lump and visible skin lesions disappeared, tumor markers normalized, and CT was negative. The authors still qualified the response as almost complete. In 2013, CT showed ovarian enlargement of uncertain significance.
results.quote:
Then she began clinical-instrumental 
follow up; she received letrozole for ten years until 2013. During 
this period the patient felt always well, we have never seen any 
disease progression.

results.finding: One patient (n=1) with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer had about 9.5 years of complete clinical remission.
results.detail: The remission interval is calculated from documented bone metastasis clearance in June 2003 to the last visit in December 2012. Annual bone scans ended in June 2005, and annual clinical follow-up continued. Flutamide ended in May 2007, after surgical castration.
results.quote: The patient has currently survived for >10 years with no development of castration resistance or signs of recurrence.

results.finding: Recurrent metastatic Ewing sarcoma (n=1): complete remission persisted for >10 years after stopping figitumumab and pegvisomant.
results.detail: The patient had previously progressed on figitumumab alone. After stopping combination therapy, she underwent serial surveillance imaging.
results.quote: The patient has remained in long-term remission (>10 years) since the discontinuation of both agents and has not received any additional therapeutic interventions.

results.finding: Pediatric superficial CIC::DUX4-rearranged sarcoma (n=5): one child was in complete remission at 69 months, with no reported recurrence.
results.detail: The qualifying case had localized supraclavicular disease and was treated surgically. The Results give 69 months, while Table 2 gives 70 months. Both exceed the five-year threshold.
results.quote:
Follow-up data, available for all cases, revealed 
complete remission at 29, 69, 16, 10, and 30 months.

results.finding: Of 1,211 patients who underwent resection of colorectal liver metastases, 192 survived 10 years without documented recurrence.
results.detail: Surveillance imaging was generally performed at least every six months, with schedules varying across the cohort. The study assessed documented recurrence and did not report a standardized symptom assessment.
results.quote: One hundred and ninety-two patients (15.6%) were 10-year survivors without recurrence

results.finding: One patient with metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma remained disease-free for five years off systemic therapy.
results.detail: The liver lesions were presumed metastases based on imaging. The later lung lesion was resected, and pathology and a matching KRAS mutation supported its pancreatic origin.
results.quote: He remained disease-free for five years until re-staging revealed a small lung nodule.

case_label = "Cancer type". Reason: The trials define eligibility by cancer type, and the laboratory and clinical results also concern particular cancers.

definition = "A treatment eliminates every malignant lineage capable of regenerating a particular advanced solid cancer at any site. In a first-strike, second-strike regimen, the first treatment reduces the size and diversity of the cancer population. A different treatment targets the survivors while their numbers are low, before regrowth. Survivors can include cells already resistant to the first drug and drug-tolerant persisters, which survive in a reversible state.". Reason: The definition gives the endpoint but omits the timing that distinguishes the proposed extinction strategy from waiting for a responding cancer to progress.

goal.need = "In Norway in 2015, metastases were recorded as a contributing cause in 6,483 deaths from solid tumours, 66.7% of the total. In previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer, median time to progression or death was 7.2 months with daraxonrasib and 3.6 months with chemotherapy. Even when tumours shrink, surviving cells can regrow. Eliminating those cells at every site, at doses patients can tolerate, would spare patients a recurrence of that cancer and further treatment for it.". Reason: The current rationale reports a cell-culture result and a small response cohort without explaining the burden of metastatic disease or what preventing recurrence would mean for patients.

add statement by H. Lee Moffitt Cancer Center and Research Institute, METTSEO protocol, 2025: "attempting to make extinct, resulting in a cure for the patient". Reason: METTSEO names extinction as a curative goal in a registered treatment protocol and distinguishes that goal from the feasibility endpoint it actually tests.

add not found: "No oncology society or cancer programme statement rejecting malignant-lineage extinction as a therapeutic goal was found.". Reason: The existing gaps concern verification of extinction and do not record the separate question of institutional disagreement about pursuing it.
add case "EGFR-mutant lung cancer". Reason: ETCTN 9903 and the DFCI-243 xenograft study both test EGFR-mutant lung cancer.
add case "Fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma". Reason: NCT04388839 defines its three-year efficacy target for metastatic fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
add case "Hormone receptor-positive breast cancer". Reason: NCT06409390 tests sequential therapy specifically in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer.
add case "Castration-sensitive prostate cancer". Reason: NCT05189457 tests a first-strike, second-strike regimen in high-risk metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer.
add case "Ewing sarcoma". Reason: The METTSEO primary feasibility objective applies to widely metastatic Ewing sarcoma.
add case "CIC-rearranged sarcoma". Reason: METTSEO separately admits patients with metastatic CIC-rearranged sarcoma, a distinct histologic diagnosis.
add case "Melanoma". Reason: The long-term immunotherapy follow-up documents both prolonged remission and late relapse in metastatic melanoma.
add case "Neuroblastoma". Reason: The GD2-directed CAR T-cell follow-up documents the duration of complete responses specifically in neuroblastoma.
add case "Colorectal cancer". Reason: CheckMate 8HW supplies disease-specific clinical evidence for metastatic colorectal cancer with high microsatellite instability or deficient mismatch repair.
add case "Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma". Reason: The daraxonrasib results concern previously treated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and require their own disease attribution.

edit m1: title = "Trichostatin A selectively kills PC9 lung-cancer persisters in a 20-hour assay."; criterion = "Plate parental PC9 cells and PC9-derived drug-tolerant persisters at equal density. Compare untreated cultures with cultures exposed to trichostatin A for 20 hours. Use flow cytometry to measure the fraction of cells with sub-G1 DNA content, a marker of cell death. The increase over the untreated control must be greater in persisters than in parental cells."; threshold_quote = "treated with the indicated TSA concentrations for 20 hours"; threshold_ref = 10; refs = [10]. Reason: Figure 4B defines a controlled, timed cell-death assay, whereas the current criterion also includes results from a different study.

edit m2: title = "TROP2 CAR T cells delay regrowth beyond 400 mm\u00b3 in an EGFR-mutant lung-cancer xenograft."; criterion = "In mice bearing DFCI-243 patient-derived tumours, give osimertinib through day 42 and introduce TROP2-directed CAR T cells or sacituzumab govitecan on day 22. Compare relapse-free survival between groups. Relapse is regrowth beyond 400 mm\u00b3 after the tumour has reached minimal residual disease. The CAR T-cell group must have longer relapse-free survival than the sacituzumab govitecan group."; threshold_quote = "prevent disease relapse, defined as when tumors reach >400 mm^{3} after achieving MRD."; threshold_ref = 12. Reason: The current criterion gives the observed relapse times and P value but leaves the treatment timing and comparison unclear.

edit m3: title = "At least half the patients complete three cycles with more than 75% of each drug\u2019s planned dose."; criterion = "In the ETCTN 9903 dose-expansion cohort with EGFR T790M-positive lung cancer, at least 50% of patients must complete three 28-day cycles while receiving more than 75% of the planned total dose of each drug, osimertinib and navitoclax."; set_by = "National Cancer Institute, ETCTN 9903, NCT02520778, registered dose-expansion feasibility endpoint."; set_by_kind = "protocol"; threshold_quote = "The proportion of patients completing 3 courses of therapy with > 75% of total dose of each drug will be quantified."; threshold_ref = 23; refs = [23, 13]. Reason: The registry requires both a minimum dose of each drug and a minimum proportion of patients completing three cycles.

edit m4: title = "The assayed EGFR mutations become undetectable in plasma after two treatment cycles."; criterion = "Evaluate patients with a detectable EGFR mutation in pretreatment plasma. Test plasma by droplet digital PCR for the known sensitizing mutation, either L858R or an exon 19 deletion, and for T790M. A complete circulating tumour DNA response requires that none of the assayed EGFR mutations be detectable after two cycles."; threshold_quote = "no detectable EGFR mutation after 2 cycles"; threshold_ref = 13. Reason: The assay tests specified EGFR variants in plasma, while the current title implies that any previously detected tumour mutation would qualify.

edit m5: title = "Non-nodal lesions disappear and all pathological nodes measure under 10 mm in short axis."; criterion = "For an overall complete response under RECIST 1.1, all non-nodal target and non-target lesions must disappear, all pathological nodes must measure less than 10 mm in short axis, initially elevated tumour markers must normalize, and no new lesion may appear. In a nonrandomized trial with response as its primary endpoint, confirm the response on repeat assessment."; threshold_quote = "Any pathological lymph nodes (whether target or non-target) must have reduction in short axis to <10 mm."; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7]. Reason: RECIST allows a previously pathological node to remain visible below 10 mm in short axis, so the title’s requirement that all lesions disappear is too strict.
